intelligence_report.confidence_rationale: Document heavily cites source materials across all substantive claims (NPL figures, capital ratios, operational metrics). Gap clarity is strong—explicitly flags missing cohort analysis, external benchmarks, and pilot data needed before pivo
intelligence_report.executive_summary: Fifteen months into the five-year plan, the board meets to decide capital allocation under strategic uncertainty. Digital operations exceed every target: mobile transactions run at 2.4× baseline, uptime holds at 99.6%, cost-to-serve has fallen 18%. The capital position remains comfortable at 16.4% CET1, providing 240 basis points above the internal floor. Two concentrations require board decisions. Real estate exposure has reached 31.2% against the 25% internal guideline. Digital lending NPLs have crossed 9% for the second time, against an original model that anticipated 6-7% steady state. The CEO assesses that cohort dynamics were insufficiently understood at strategy approval and recommends lowering the digital revenue target from 18% to 16% by FY28, pivoting the product mix from unsecured consumer to secured SME lending. The board must set risk tolerance bands and decision criteria for management to operate within, rather than commit to a single path without adequate cohort-level data.
intelligence_report.framing: Board Chair and Chief Executive Officer · 25 June 2025

recommendations.text: Board to set explicit risk tolerance band for digital lending NPLs (acceptable range: 6-9%, 8-11%, or other) by end of meeting, determining whether current performance is within strategic tolerance or requires pivot.
CEO to commission external credit portfolio review and digital lending benchmark study, delivering cohort-level root cause analysis for 9% NPL rate and peer comparables by end Q4 2025.
CFO to model capital implications and ROE outcomes for all three digital strategy options (maintain target, reduce target, pivot product) at 8-11% NPL range, presenting to board by August 2025.
CRO to establish monthly digital portfolio review cadence until NPL trajectory stabilizes below 8% or product pivot is approved, reporting material changes to board within 48 hours.
CEO to establish active real estate concentration management protocol, preventing drift beyond 32% and presenting quarterly reduction path to restore 25% guideline by end FY26.
Board Risk Committee to review secured SME digital lending business case and pilot plan before commitment, assessing whether economics and execution risk are superior to fixing current product.
CFO to reserve 100-150 basis points CET1 headroom for opportunistic deployment as specified in capital allocation framework, withholding deployment until digital strategy uncertainty resolves.
Board Chair to convene extraordinary strategy session if Q4 digital cohort shows NPLs at or above 9% again, escalating pivot decision timeline.
